actors.name: Kela (the document does not distinguish caseworker from automated system)

nodes.name: Household with small income needs help with housing costs
nodes.description: Trigger: a person or household on a small income with housing costs turns to Kela for general housing allowance (yleinen asumistuki).

evidence.quote: If you have a small income, Kela can grant you general housing allowance.
The purpose of the general housing allowance is to help you with your housing costs.

nodes.name: Estimate allowance with Kela calculator (optional)
nodes.description: The applicant can use the housing allowance calculator on Kela's website to estimate the amount before applying.

evidence.quote: You can use the housing allowance calculator on Kela’s website to estimate how much housing allowance you can get.

nodes.name: Choose application channel
nodes.description: The applicant chooses between applying online in OmaKela or on a paper application form.

evidence.quote: Apply for general housing allowance online:
You can also apply by filling in an application form that you can get from a service point or from Kela’s website:

nodes.name: Log in to OmaKela
nodes.description: The applicant logs in to the OmaKela e-service with online banking credentials or a mobile ID.

evidence.quote: You must log in to OmaKela. You need online banking credentials or a mobile ID.

nodes.name: Complete online application and declare all income
nodes.description: The applicant fills in and submits the online application and must declare all of their income.

evidence.quote: Apply for general housing allowance online:
You must declare all of your income in the application for housing allowance.

nodes.name: Send supporting documents online
nodes.description: The applicant sends the supporting documents listed in the application online.

evidence.quote: Check the application for a list of the supporting documents you need to send with the application.
The supporting documents can also be sent online.

nodes.name: Obtain and fill in paper application form
nodes.description: The applicant gets the application form from a service point or Kela's website and fills it in, with the supporting documents listed in it.

evidence.quote: You can also apply by filling in an application form that you can get from a service point or from Kela’s website:
Check the application for a list of the supporting documents you need to send with the application.

nodes.name: Post paper application to Kela
nodes.description: The applicant sends the paper application to Kela by post (Kela, PL 10, 00056 KELA).

evidence.quote: If you apply for a Kela benefit on an application form, send the application to Kela by post.
Kela’s address is: Kela PL 10 00056 KELA

nodes.name: Receive application
nodes.description: Kela receives the application; the date of receipt matters for the retroactive start of the allowance.

evidence.quote: if you want to get the allowance from January onward, Kela must get your application before the end of February.

nodes.name: Limit start of allowance to one month before application
nodes.description: Kela applies the rule that the allowance can be applied for retroactively for up to one month.

evidence.quote: You can apply for housing allowance retroactively for up to one month.
if you want to get the allowance from January onward, Kela must get your application before the end of February.

nodes.name: Determine household
nodes.description: Kela establishes who forms the household (people living permanently in the same house or apartment), which can be one person or many.

evidence.quote: A household means people who live permanently in the same house or apartment.
Kela can pay general housing allowance to one person or to a household of many people.

nodes.name: Check dwelling type
nodes.description: Kela checks that the home is a rented, right-of-occupancy or part-ownership home and not an apartment or single-family home owned by the applicant.

evidence.quote: You may qualify for general housing allowance if you live • in a rented house or apartment • in a right-of-occupancy home • in a part-ownership home.
You cannot get general housing allowance if you own the apartment or single-family home that you live in.

nodes.name: Check student status
nodes.description: Kela checks whether a student applicant lives with their own child or their partner's child, which is required for students.

evidence.quote: If you are a student, you can get general housing allowance only if you live with your own child or your partner’s child.

nodes.name: Check for another housing benefit
nodes.description: Kela checks that no other kind of housing benefit (pensioners' housing allowance, students' housing supplement, conscripts' housing assistance) is paid at the same time.

evidence.quote: You can usually be paid only one kind of housing benefit at a time.
You can also get housing allowance for pensioners, housing supplement for students and housing assistance for conscripts from Kela.

nodes.name: Determine acceptable housing costs by dwelling type
nodes.description: Kela takes rent (rented or part-ownership home) or residence charge (right-of-occupancy home) as housing costs, limited to costs defined as acceptable in law.

evidence.quote: a rented house or apartment: rent plus water and heating costs • a right-of-occupancy home: residence charge plus water and heating costs
It only covers housing costs that are defined as acceptable in law.

nodes.name: Add separately paid water and heating costs within limits
nodes.description: Water and heating costs count only if not included in rent or residence charge: water up to EUR 20 per person per month; heating up to EUR 46 per month for one person, plus EUR 16 per additional person.

evidence.quote: Water and heating costs are accepted as housing costs if they are not included in your rent or residence charge and you have to pay them separately.
Kela accepts water charges of up to EUR 20 per person and per month.
If you live alone in a single-person household, Kela accepts heating costs of up to EUR 46 per month.
this limit for acceptable heating costs increases by EUR 16 for each additional person.

nodes.name: Determine legal maximum housing costs
nodes.description: Kela determines the legal maximum housing costs from the number of adults and children in the home and the cost-of-living category of the municipality.

evidence.quote: The maximum amount of housing costs depends on how many adults and children live in the same home and which municipality the home is located in.
Finnish municipalities are divided into categories according to the cost of living there.

nodes.name: Compare actual housing costs with legal maximum
nodes.description: Kela checks whether the housing costs exceed the maximum housing costs defined in law.

evidence.quote: If your housing costs are higher than the maximum housing costs defined in law, Kela will use the maximum housing costs to calculate how much housing allowance you can get.

nodes.name: Use maximum housing costs
nodes.description: When actual costs exceed the legal maximum, Kela calculates the allowance from the maximum housing costs.

evidence.quote: Kela does not use Maija’s actual rent (EUR 800) when calculating her housing allowance because her rent is higher than the maximum housing costs accepted for a person living alone in Helsinki.

nodes.name: Use actual housing costs
nodes.description: When actual costs are below the legal maximum, Kela calculates the allowance from the actual housing costs.

evidence.quote: Kela calculates how much housing allowance Tommi can get based on his rent (EUR 291) because Tommi’s rent is lower than the maximum housing costs accepted for a person living alone in Kemi.

nodes.name: Retrieve wage data from Incomes Register
nodes.description: Kela can fetch information on wages and salaries paid to the applicant from the Incomes Register.

evidence.quote: Kela can also get information on wages and salaries paid to you from the Incomes Register.

nodes.name: Determine income and assets that count
nodes.description: Kela takes into account earned income, assets, capital income and various benefits of the household.

evidence.quote: earned income (for example wages or salary) • assets (for example shares and money in your bank account) • capital income (for example rental income or interest on deposits)
various benefits (for example unemployment benefits, sickness allowance and daily allowances for parents).

nodes.name: Disregard excluded benefits and child's income
nodes.description: Kela leaves out certain benefits (e.g. social assistance, child benefit) and the income and assets of a child under 18 in the household.

evidence.quote: certain benefits (for example social assistance, child benefit, provider supplement to the study grant or informal care allowance)
the income and assets of a child under the age of 18 who is a member of the household.

nodes.name: Check whether income is stable
nodes.description: Kela decides whether the income stays the same or varies from month to month.

evidence.quote: Your income may be the same every month or it may be different from one month to the next.

nodes.name: Calculate continuous income
nodes.description: If income will stay the same for 3 months after the grant or review, Kela calculates a continuous income.

evidence.quote: Kela will calculate a continuous income for you in the following situation: your income will stay the same for 3 months after you have been granted housing allowance or after your housing allowance has been reviewed.

nodes.name: Calculate average income over next 12 months
nodes.description: If income varies month to month, Kela calculates an average income based on the next 12 months.

evidence.quote: If your income is different from one month to the next, Kela will calculate an average income for you based on your income for the next 12 months.

nodes.name: Determine basic deductible
nodes.description: Kela sets the basic deductible from household size (adults and children) and gross monthly household income; higher income gives a larger deductible.

evidence.quote: The amount of the basic deductible depends on • how many adults and children live in the household • the gross household income per month.
The bigger the income is, the larger the deductible.

nodes.name: Deduct basic deductible from housing costs
nodes.description: Kela subtracts the basic deductible from the housing costs used in the calculation (maximum or actual).

evidence.quote: First, Kela deducts the basic deductible from your housing costs.
Kela deducts a basic deductible from the housing costs when calculating the amount of housing allowance Kela can pay.

nodes.name: Calculate allowance as 70% of remainder
nodes.description: The allowance equals 70% of the remaining acceptable housing costs (the applicant always pays at least 30%).

evidence.quote: The housing allowance you can get is equal to 70% of the remaining amount of acceptable housing costs.
Housing allowance can cover up to 70% of your housing costs.

nodes.name: Grant allowance
nodes.description: Kela decides to grant the allowance, setting the benefit amount, the reasons and the payment date given in the decision notice.

evidence.quote: The decision notice will tell you how much benefit you get, the reasons for granting it and when it will be paid to you.

nodes.name: Send decision notice on grant
nodes.description: Once the application is processed, Kela sends the decision notice via OmaKela or by post to the home address.

evidence.quote: As soon as Kela has processed your application, you will get a decision notice in the OmaKela e-service or by post to your home address.

nodes.name: Reject application
nodes.description: Kela decides to reject the application (for example when eligibility conditions are not met).

evidence.quote: You will get a decision notice also if Kela rejects your application.

nodes.name: Send decision notice on rejection
nodes.description: Kela sends a decision notice to the applicant also when the application is rejected.

evidence.quote: You will get a decision notice also if Kela rejects your application.
As soon as Kela has processed your application, you will get a decision notice in the OmaKela e-service or by post to your home address.

nodes.name: Read decision notice and check it
nodes.description: The applicant reads the decision notice and decides whether it is correct or wrong.

evidence.quote: If you think that the decision you got from Kela is wrong, you can appeal to have it changed.

nodes.name: Contact Kela first about questions
nodes.description: If the applicant has questions about a decision, they are asked to contact Kela first.

evidence.quote: If you have questions, please contact Kela first.

nodes.name: Appeal the decision
nodes.description: The applicant appeals the decision following the instructions that come with every decision notice.

evidence.quote: You get instructions on how to appeal the decision with every decision notice you get from Kela.
If you think that the decision you got from Kela is wrong, you can appeal to have it changed.

nodes.name: Appeal lodged (handling not described in this document)
nodes.description: End of what this document covers on appeals; who handles the appeal and how is not described.

evidence.quote: If you think that the decision you got from Kela is wrong, you can appeal to have it changed.

nodes.name: Choose payee: own bank account or landlord
nodes.description: The recipient can ask Kela to pay the allowance directly to the landlord instead of to their own bank account.

evidence.quote: You can also ask Kela to pay your housing allowance directly to your landlord.

nodes.name: Pay allowance to recipient's bank account
nodes.description: Kela pays the allowance to the recipient's bank account on the first banking day of the month.

evidence.quote: Kela pays the general housing allowance to your bank account on the first banking day of the month.

nodes.name: Pay allowance directly to landlord
nodes.description: On the recipient's request, Kela pays the allowance directly to the landlord (timing not stated).

evidence.quote: You can also ask Kela to pay your housing allowance directly to your landlord.

nodes.name: Application rejected
nodes.description: End state: application rejected and decision notice received.

evidence.quote: You will get a decision notice also if Kela rejects your application.

nodes.name: Annual review of allowance
nodes.description: Kela reviews the housing allowance once a year.

evidence.quote: Kela reviews the housing allowance once a year.

nodes.name: Early review after change in circumstances
nodes.description: Kela can review the allowance sooner if the recipient's circumstances change.

evidence.quote: Kela can review the allowance sooner if your circumstances change.

nodes.name: Report change in circumstances to Kela
nodes.description: The recipient reports changes in housing, income, work or family circumstances online in OmaKela, by phone or at a service point; it is their responsibility to keep Kela's information correct.

evidence.quote: Remember to report such changes to Kela.
You can do it online in the OmaKela e-service, by phone or by visiting a Kela service point.
Remember to tell Kela if your income increases or decreases.
It is up to you to make sure that Kela has the correct information.

nodes.name: Request to stop payment of allowance
nodes.description: The recipient can stop the payment of benefits in the OmaKela e-service.

evidence.quote: send messages • report changes • stop the payment of benefits.

nodes.name: Payment of allowance stopped
nodes.description: End state: payment stopped at the recipient's initiative.

evidence.quote: send messages • report changes • stop the payment of benefits.
